name: George Norris, chart and views of Liverpool Island (Bouvet) and Thompson's Island, from the log of the smack Sprightly, Nov.-Dec. 1825; copy in the Hydrographic Department, published as 'Bouvet Island. Copies of Sketches from the Log of the Sprightly, Captain Norris', The Geographical Journal, December 1928
holding: plate scanned by Antique Maps and Prints (stock P-6-110763), served as a deep-zoom image, 8267 x 10680
image_note: The local raster is the chart part of the plate only, stitched from the deep-zoom tiles at full resolution (https://images.antiquemapsandprints.com/scansfcg/P-6-110763.dzi, level 14, columns 14-31, rows 20-36): 4572 x 4318 px, its origin at x 3556, y 5080 of the full plate. Pixel coordinates below are in that crop.
licence: the drawing is Norris's of 1825; the RGS printed it in 1928 by permission of the Admiralty. Used here as a source, not reproduced
note: The discoverer's own chart: Norris saw the island in December 1825, from the Sprightly, a week after landing on Bouvet, which he took for a new island and called Liverpool Island. He drew Thompson's Island in plan, a small open outline in four strokes, with the Chimnies (two rocks) and a third rock to its south-east. The same sheet has his profile of the island, a long low shape with a peak at one end. Chosen by Etienne in November 2026, the plan over the profile, at the chart's own scale, placed by its offset from Liverpool Island. No other depiction found: later charts, to 1943, draw a dot.
graticule_note: Minutes of latitude on the right (55', 54 S, 5', 10', 15' at y 684, 1108, 1543, 1994, 2422 near x 3000-3600), 86.9 px per minute; meridians 5 E and 6 E at x 519 and 3632, 51.9 px per minute of longitude, a ratio of cos 53.4, so the sheet is drawn at one scale in km (about 47 px/km). The lines are not quite straight on the paper, so positions are read against the lines nearest each island: Thompson's Island at 53 55.9 S 5 29.6 E (the charted position, 53 56 S 5 30 E), Liverpool Island's centre at 54 14.4 S 5 0.7 E. The real Bouvet is at 54 25 S 3 22 E: the whole chart sits about 1.6 degrees east and 11' north.
extraction_note: --mode dark at grey 100, with the 55' parallel and the 5 30 E meridian that cross the island painted out, and --join 14 to close Norris's four strokes, whose gaps run up to 25 px, into one ring before the island is chosen. Stable from threshold 90 to 120 and join 12 to 18: 119 x 107 px, about 7,170 px.
